office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Jim Lucas
incumbent.summary: Jim Lucas, a Seymour business owner and Marine Corps veteran, has represented House District 69 since 2012 [3]. He was reelected in 2024 with 68.7% of the vote [4].
record: Committees: Financial Institutions, Veterans Affairs and Public Safety, and Public Policy, according to his caucus biography [3].

2023: Authored a law creating an optional, state-funded 40-hour firearms training course for school staff who are allowed to carry [5]. 2024: Authored HEA 1142, creating the Hoosier First Responder Medal of Honor [6]. 2025: Co-authored HEA 1114, raising penalties for unlicensed drivers who cause injury or death [7].

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) [8]; the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) [9]; and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) [10].

race_context: House District 69 includes portions of Bartholomew, Jackson, Scott and Washington counties, according to the House Republican caucus [3]; The Indiana Citizen describes it as representing Seymour, Brownstown and Salem [11]. (It does not include Jennings County, which is mostly in House District 67.)
Lucas and Chris Bowen were each the only declared candidate in their party's May 5, 2026 primary [4]. Tyler J. Henkle is on the ballot as an independent, making this a three-candidate race [2].
No debate or candidate forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Seven-term Republican incumbent from Seymour seeking reelection [3, 4].
background: U.S. Marine Corps veteran and small-business owner (The Awning Guy, Inc.); formerly served on the Seymour City Council [3].
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary [4].

items: His caucus biography lists "protecting the right to bear arms" among his top priorities, along with jobs, fiscal integrity and education [3].
On school staff firearms training: "I want our schools to have every available option to boost security and be a deterrent to anyone looking to do harm" [5].
Told students in 2024 that more gun laws would not stop people "who aren't being stopped by the hundreds of existing laws right now" [12].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No public statements about his 2026 opponents were found.
plans: No 2026 campaign platform was found beyond his caucus biography.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: 2025–2026 bills he authored beyond HEA 1114 co-authorship were not verified.

candidates.summary: Democratic nominee from Seymour who filed in January 2026 as part of the Indiana Rural Summit coalition's candidate filing event [11].
path_to_ballot: Filed Jan. 7, 2026 with the Indiana Rural Summit, a nonprofit that trains Democratic candidates from rural and small-town Indiana [11]; unopposed in the May 5 Democratic primary [4].

items: Said she was motivated to run by the legislature's passage of laws restricting abortion [11].
Cited laws she said limit access to the ballot box as a reason for running [11].

on_incumbent: Said Lucas does not listen to constituents' concerns and "just does what he wants" (as paraphrased by The Indiana Citizen); said, "Even if I don't agree, if that's what most of my constituents want, that's the way I'll vote" [11].
plans: "I just want to be the voice for the people" [11].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: No campaign website or detailed platform was found.
Unverified: iVoterGuide lists an endorsement from Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and education at Texas A&M-Commerce; Blue Voter Guide pages conflict on endorsements.
